markdown_report:
Select a norm-controlled current-item readout gate after correcting padding execution. At 10% progress, this remains a feasible GRU4Rec experiment; fixed-weight fusion is its essential architectural control.

Starting-point insights: (1) Recurrent states and observed-item embeddings may complement each other, but their scales and coordinates need not align. (2) Sampled training errors span 1.4–4.75%; they do not establish validation quality. (3) Unpadded replay changes scores by up to 2.38, preventing causal interpretation of existing deletion diagnostics.

Related-work insights: (1) PyTorch packing excludes padding only after chronological compaction [1]. (2) BPR-max emphasizes competitive negatives, with differentiable negative weights and score regularization [2]. (3) NARM, HGN and Highway Networks establish close architectural ancestry [5–7]; originality is incremental. (4) Sampled metrics and adaptive validation selection constrain generalization claims [8–10].

The framework separates execution correctness → trustworthy interventions; ranking objectives → candidate separation; contextual readout → recent/history balance; evaluation discipline → credible selection. Execution correctness precedes architectural interpretation.

Three atomic proposals follow. Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment includes a strength and limitation.

| Proposal | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Regularized BPR-max [2] | 2: established; little novelty | 7: practical; transfer uncertain | 4: competitive ranking; indirect intent link | 7: residual errors; training evidence only | 4: localized objective; sampling controls required |
| **Current-item readout gate** [5–7] | 3: focused adaptation; close precedents | 6: testable; latest-item shortcuts possible | 7: recent-specific evidence; needs unobserved | 6: residual errors; causal evidence absent | 4: small module; execution/export controls required |
| Joint title encoder [4] | 5: attribute distinctions; established fusion | 7: specification cues; sparse supervision | 8: finer relevance; compatibility unverifiable | 5: discrimination; no text diagnostic | 6: joint network; token pipeline required |

The selected gate targets two user failures: broad associations displacing specific matches, and insufficient weight on recent coherent interests. Movies’ 4.75% sampled ranking error supplies a model-facing target. These are hypotheses; one latest-item branch cannot establish coherent intent, ownership needs or compatibility.

Compute ordinary features h and projected observed-item embedding p. Clip p’s norm to at most ||h||, obtaining u; then f=(1−g)⊙h+g⊙u, with g=0.2σ(W[h;u]+b), initially 0.01. Consequently ||f−h||≤0.4||h||, initially ≤0.02||h||. Even these bounds cannot prevent near-tied ranking reversals.

Compare the corrected baseline, fixed g=0.01, and learned gate with identical projection and norm control. Test BPR-max separately using matched candidate pools; λ=0 isolates aggregation from score regularization. Additional scalar controls and combined changes remain budget-dependent.

Predeclare comparison order, practical gain threshold, category guardrails and compute allocation. Select solely by pinned sampled-candidate macro validation HR@10. Use paired user intervals only when host outputs permit; they neither cover retraining variability nor correct adaptive selection. Deploy one checkpoint per category.

References: [1] PyTorch; [2] Hidasi–Karatzoglou; [3] Mamba4Rec; [4] MARS; [5] NARM; [6] HGN; [7] Highway Networks; [8] Krichene–Rendle; [9] Bouthillier et al.; [10] Cawley–Talbot. Links appear below.

idea.description: Add a coordinate-wise gate combining ordinary GRU4Rec recommendation features with a norm-controlled projection of the currently observed item's embedding. Train every component jointly within one network per category. Establish padding-invariant execution first, compare learned gating against matched fixed-weight fusion, and isolate this architectural change from a separate regularized BPR-max experiment.
idea.motivation: The gate explicitly targets two reported user-facing failures: broadly related recommendations displacing specific matches, and recent coherent interests receiving insufficient weight relative to broad historical interests. The observed-item branch supplies direct recent evidence while the recurrent branch retains multi-item context. This mechanism addresses those failures as hypotheses rather than established remedies: a latest purchase is not necessarily a current need or a coherent interest. The model-facing target is residual sampled positive/negative ranking error, especially 4.75% in Movies_and_TV and 3.42% in Electronics. These training measurements do not establish harmful memory, validation gains, or full-catalog recommendation quality. Existing deletion results are confounded by padded recurrent updates. Ownership needs, equipment compatibility, project intent and desired quantities remain unobserved.
idea.implementation_notes:
Integrate into the supplied corrected GRU4Rec rather than replacing its backbone. Inherit and record its dimensions, scoring function, score activation, dropout, optimizer, initialization, negative sampler, loss reduction and checkpoint-selection schedule unless explicitly testing one of them. The actual baseline source and numeric hyperparameters are absent from the prompt; this is an integration specification, not a runnable replacement pipeline. Resolve inherited values from the host baseline before execution and record every effective configuration.

First verify padding semantics. If the corrected baseline already skips padded recurrence, retain it. Otherwise compact real items in chronological order, pack only nonempty rows, run the existing GRU, unpack, and scatter outputs back to their original valid positions. Never pack the original left-padded tensor using valid lengths. Preserve multilayer hidden-state ordering, baseline dropout placement and scoring behavior. Empty histories produce zero features while preserving any baseline scoring bias. A recurrence correction requires retraining; never reinterpret old checkpoints under changed execution. Verify identical histories under additional leading padding, separate/batched execution, repeated calls and batch permutation in evaluation mode. Use dtype-appropriate declared tolerances, initially atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-5 for float32 scores; investigate discrepancies rather than silently relaxing tolerances. Measure more than the single history used in the supplied audit, including empty, singleton, mixed-length and full-length rows. Separately compare production readout against an independent maximum-nonzero-index gather from the same captured feature tensor.

Let h_t be the baseline recommendation feature of dimension D and p_t=P(item_emb(sequence_t)). Use an identity projection when dimensions match; otherwise use a bias-free trainable linear projection initialized with Xavier uniform weights and record that choice. Identity initialization does not establish coordinate alignment. Define rho_t=min(1, ||h_t||_2/(||p_t||_2+1e-8)) and u_t=rho_t*p_t, with norms accumulated in float32. Differentiate through the norm-control computation; do not detach it. Thus ||u_t||_2<=||h_t||_2, including u_t=0 when h_t=0. Define g_t=0.2*sigmoid(W_h*h_t+W_u*u_t+b) and f_t=(1-g_t)*h_t+g_t*u_t. Initialize W_h=W_u=0 and the single total bias b=log(0.01/(0.2-0.01))=log(0.05/0.95), giving g_t=0.01 exactly before optimization. The gate cap alone would only imply ||f_t-h_t||_2<=0.2||p_t-h_t||_2 without norm control. With the proposed norm control, ||f_t-h_t||_2<=0.4||h_t||_2; initially the bound is 0.02||h_t||_2 because the gate is uniformly 0.01. These are feature-space bounds, not guarantees of unchanged scores or ranks. Candidate-embedding norms can amplify score changes, and near ties can reverse after arbitrarily small feature changes.

Apply this readout after the baseline recommendation-feature transformation, preserving its existing dropout locations. Do not feed f_t back into the GRU. Zero padded features and use f_t wherever the baseline uses recommendation features, retaining the same candidate scorer. This is one jointly trained feature computation; there are no independently fitted branches or separately combined recommendation scores. Norm control adds no trainable scale parameters. LayerNorm is an alternative control, not an additional simultaneous change: normalizing h would alter the baseline, and independently learned normalization gains could restore branch imbalance.

Predeclare the initial experiment order: execution-correct ordinary baseline; fixed g=0.01 with the same projection and norm control; learned coordinate-wise gate with baseline loss. Initialize shared parameters identically across these configurations, explicitly copying common initial tensors where needed; seed equality alone does not guarantee identical draws after adding parameters. Replay identical training examples and candidate pools. The fixed-weight control trains its projection jointly and tests whether input-dependent gating improves over adding the branch itself. A later learned global scalar and input-dependent scalar can distinguish global weighting from coordinate-wise adaptation. A small prespecified fixed-weight grid can test whether a tuned constant matches the learned gate, but each additional training run counts against the budget and validation-comparison limit. If these controls are unrun, restrict claims accordingly. Do not claim superiority over tuned fixed fusion from the single g=0.01 control.

Test regularized BPR-max as a separate objective experiment on the ordinary corrected backbone, without the gate. If the baseline already uses equivalent BPR-max, omit duplicate configurations. Compare ordinary mean pairwise -logsigmoid against BPR-max using identical examples, candidate pools, multiplicities, collision masks, initialization, architecture, score activation, optimizer and update count. Baseline loss semantics must remain separately documented if they differ from mean BPR. For a minimal explicit candidate-pool setting, use K=64 uniform additional negatives per supervised position and lambda=0.1 for the regularized variant; also use lambda=0 to distinguish aggregation from negative-score regularization. These are proposed settings, not values inherited from the absent baseline or guaranteed optima. If the matched objective controls cannot fit the allocated compute, defer this direction instead of changing sampling and loss together and calling the result loss-only.

For negative scores s_j, use w=softmax(s_j), loss=-log(sum_j w_j*sigmoid(s_pos-s_j))+lambda*sum_j w_j*s_j^2. Compute the first term with log_softmax, logsigmoid and logsumexp; accumulate in float32. Differentiate through w in both terms. Apply the host scorer's configured activation consistently before this loss. The weighted negative-score penalty is distinct from parameter weight decay. Record reduction over candidates and valid positions because loss scale changes effective optimization.

If using the proposed filtered pools, exclude padding, the target ID and the user's known training positives, and sample uniformly without replacement from the remaining training catalog. Never consult validation/test positives for exclusions. Deduplicate candidates identically for both objectives. For rows with fewer than K eligible items, use all eligible items, mask unused slots before softmax, and exclude rows with no eligible negatives while reporting their count. Construct exclusions using actual training user identity in the family-specific sampler, not by inferring users from anonymous diagnostic rows. This filtering and uniqueness deliberately differ from official GRU4Rec sampling, which uses in-batch targets plus additional replacement draws, retains multiplicities and does not exclude consumed items. Do not describe the filtered adaptation as an exact reproduction of the official implementation. The official recommendation of approximately 2,048 additional samples motivates a later compute-dependent comparison, not a required default for this experiment.

Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb, predict_score(features, items), and the host ModelView contract, including supported candidate tensor shapes. log2feats must return the actual gated features when that architecture is trained, aligned to original positions. Read the greatest nonpadding index, never count-1. Handle zero-width histories explicitly if the host supports them. Save architecture variant, dimensions, projection initialization, norm-control epsilon, gate cap and initialization, dropout, score activation and state_dict together. Update the embedded predictor writer using the identical recurrence, projection, norm control, gate, readout and scorer. Verify reloaded predictor scores against the selected in-memory model on identical histories and candidates. Each of Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl loads exactly one selected checkpoint; comparison configurations are never combined at inference.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning measured metrics and metric_definitions. view.model remains the actual trained nn.Module; preserve user_train, meta_data and review_data interfaces without fabricating unavailable fields. Keep loader tuples (None, sequence, positive, negative), with tensors B x L. Preserve valid-pair margins, error rates and their existing definitions. Add nonpadding gate quantiles, ||p_t||, ||h_t||, norm-clipping frequency, and ||f_t-h_t||/||h_t||. Also measure ||g_t*u_t||/||(1-g_t)*h_t|| using actual coordinate-wise contributions. Report denominators, zero-norm counts and undefined ratios explicitly. Gate values alone do not measure branch influence, and neither feature bounds nor gate values demonstrate improved intent matching.

After padding checks pass, rerun the existing matched history interventions, preserving their populations, candidates, perturbation seed and definitions. Keep diagnostic batches fixed across comparisons where the host permits. Separate recurrent-state sensitivity from final gated-feature sensitivity. Do not equate greater recency sensitivity with improved recommendations: the supplied measurements do not establish insufficient recency after correcting padding. Track training-frequency slices and history-length slices with explicit counts to investigate latest-item memorization or head-item shortcuts. Near-zero mean embedding cosine does not establish recommendation diversity. Anonymous diagnostic rows are not independent users; missing metadata and unavailable export measurements remain explicitly unavailable rather than fabricated.

Use the native full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five real training users per category to inspect whether recent-specific recommendations become more compelling and whether duplicate-function or unsupported-compatibility rejections increase. Record these judgments only if the existing simulator supplies them. Do not invent simulator traits or convert qualitative judgments into validation improvements. The gate may worsen redundant purchase suggestions, amplify accidental recent actions, or suppress useful persistent preferences. It cannot resolve compatibility or quantities from item IDs alone. A deferred title/description encoder could supply specification cues, but would still require interaction supervision and could learn textual shortcuts; no pretrained weights are permitted.

Before requesting any validation results, record comparison order, maximum configurations, GPU-time allocations and acceptance thresholds. A concrete initial plan permits at most six configurations including the corrected baseline, caps baseline plus initial architectural controls at 21,600 GPU-seconds, objective comparisons at 12,960, and diagnostics, integration checks and failures at 8,640, totaling 43,200. Stop or defer configurations when their allocation is exhausted; do not require completing every proposed experiment. Use a practical macro gain threshold delta=0.005 and reject a replacement if any category HR@10 decreases by more than 0.01. These are prespecified operational choices, not statistically established thresholds. Selection still uses the unchanged official macro validation HR@10; these guardrails govern whether evidence warrants replacing the incumbent. Record every attempted configuration, elapsed GPU time and available paired outcomes, including failures and inconclusive results. A combined gate/BPR-max experiment is deferred unless separately beneficial changes and remaining predeclared capacity justify it.

If the host exposes per-user validation hits, retain paired incumbent/challenger indicators with the same user histories and candidate lists. With analysis seed 42, perform 10,000 paired bootstrap resamples: sample 200 user pairs with replacement within each category, compute each category's mean hit difference, and average the four category differences equally. Share sampled indices across models. If reliable identities overlap across categories, use a prespecified identity-cluster bootstrap preserving those cross-category dependencies; independent category resampling would then be inappropriate. Report the resampling scheme, percentile interval and observed difference. If required identities or hit indicators are unavailable, mark the interval unavailable without modifying the evaluator. One hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. Intervals condition on fitted checkpoints, histories, fixed candidates and seed 42; they exclude retraining, candidate resampling, split and seed variability. They do not correct adaptive validation selection, and bootstrap repetitions are not independent training runs. No significance claim is required for these exploratory comparisons.

Keep DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], artifacts beneath the trial directory, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum epochs 200, and exactly 200 batches per completed epoch. Preserve supplied splits, all category routes, the pinned evaluator and native training-user recommendations. Use single-GPU execution; every training run, diagnostic, integration check and failure consumes the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Measure synchronized step time, examples per second and peak GPU memory for representative batches rather than assuming packing improves speed. Select using macro validation HR@10 with 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42. Describe this specifically as sampled-candidate performance; full-catalog rankings can differ. No hidden tests, other-trial checkpoints, extra datasets, pretrained weights, unavailable metadata, independent fitted scores, ensembles or checkpoint averaging.
idea.pseudocode:
DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']
set_preprocessing_seed(0)
record_prespecified_configuration_order_thresholds_and_gpu_allocations()

# Integration specification: reuse the corrected host GRU4Rec and sampler.
# No filesystem inspection or training is performed in this writing call.
def log2feats(sequence):
    valid = sequence.ne(0)
    # If correction is needed: compact chronological valid items, pack nonempty
    # rows, run ordinary GRU, unpack, scatter to original positions.
    h = padding_safe_baseline_recommendation_features(sequence)
    if variant in {'fixed_readout', 'gated_readout'}:
        p = current_item_projection(item_emb(sequence))
        h_norm = vector_norm(h.float(), dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        p_norm = vector_norm(p.float(), dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        rho = minimum(ones_like(h_norm), h_norm / (p_norm + 1e-8))
        u = p * rho.to(p.dtype)  # Differentiable; no detach.
        if variant == 'fixed_readout':
            g = 0.01
        else:
            g = 0.2 * sigmoid(gate_h(h) + gate_u(u) + gate_bias)
        h = (1.0 - g) * h + g * u
    return where(valid[..., None], h, zeros_like(h))

# gate_h and gate_u have no internal biases; use one explicit gate_bias.
# Initially weights=0; gate_bias=log(0.01/(0.2-0.01)).
# Projection: identity if dimensions match, otherwise bias-free Xavier uniform.

def final_features(sequence, features):
    if sequence.shape[1] == 0:
        return zeros_for_supported_empty_history_batch()
    positions = arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
    index = where(sequence.ne(0), positions[None, :], -1).amax(dim=1)
    result = gather_time(features, index.clamp_min(0))
    return where(index[:, None].ge(0), result, zeros_like(result))

# All comparisons train separate configurations; their scores are never combined.
for configuration in prespecified_affordable_configurations:
    for category in FOUR_REQUIRED_CATEGORIES:
        set_training_seed(42)
        model = construct_host_gru4rec(configuration)
        restore_identical_common_initial_tensors_for_matched_controls(model)
        for epoch in range(at_most_200):
            if insufficient_budget_for_completed_epoch():
                break
            for batch_index in range(200):
                batch = family_specific_sample_batch_with_training_user_context()
                _, sequence, positive, negative = batch.compatibility_tuple
                features = model.log2feats(sequence)
                if configuration.is_matched_objective_control:
                    # Replay identical candidate pools across matched objectives.
                    candidates, candidate_mask = training_only_uniform_unique_pool(
                        user_ids=batch.training_user_ids, K=64,
                        exclude_padding=True, exclude_targets=True,
                        exclude_known_training_positives=True)
                    s_pos, s_neg = model.score_training_candidates(
                        features, positive, candidates)
                    s_pos, s_neg = s_pos.float(), s_neg.float()
                    valid = host_valid_positive_positions(sequence, positive)
                    valid &= candidate_mask.any(dim=-1)
                    # Restrict to valid rows before softmax: no all-masked rows.
                    a = masked_select_rows(s_pos, valid)
                    b = masked_select_rows(s_neg, valid)
                    m = masked_select_rows(candidate_mask, valid)
                    if configuration.objective == 'mean_bpr':
                        loss = masked_candidate_mean(
                            -logsigmoid(a[..., None] - b), m).mean()
                    else:
                        log_w = log_softmax(b.masked_fill(~m, -inf), dim=-1)
                        ranking = -logsumexp(
                            log_w + logsigmoid(a[..., None] - b), dim=-1)
                        safe_b = where(m, b, zeros_like(b))
                        penalty = configuration.lambda_reg * (
                            log_w.exp() * safe_b.square()).sum(dim=-1)
                        loss = (ranking + penalty).mean()
                    # Explicitly skip and count batches with no valid rows.
                else:
                    mask = host_valid_supervision_mask(sequence, positive, negative)
                    loss = host_baseline_loss(
                        model, features, positive, negative, mask)
                host_optimizer_step_if_valid(loss)
                charge_elapsed_gpu_time_including_failures()
            apply_unchanged_host_validation_and_checkpoint_schedule()
        save_one_selected_checkpoint_with_complete_architecture(category)
    write_matching_embedded_predictor_with_all_four_routes()
    verify_padding_readout_batch_and_reloaded_predictor_agreement()
    run_required_diagnostics_returning_metrics_and_metric_definitions()
    obtain_unchanged_host_sampled_macro_validation()
    record_all_results_and_available_paired_user_hits()
    apply_prespecified_delta_and_category_guardrails()
    stop_if_budget_or_comparison_limit_reached()

# If host supplies reliable user-level hits, estimate paired uncertainty with
# 10,000 seed-42 resamples, preserving cross-category identity dependencies.
# Otherwise report uncertainty unavailable. Never bootstrap anonymous rows as users.
# Final predictor loads exactly one selected checkpoint per category.

originality.positive: The norm-controlled, bounded observed-item readout is a focused GRU4Rec adaptation with explicit fixed-fusion controls and falsifiable execution guarantees.
originality.negative: Highway interpolation, recent/global representation combinations and recommendation gates have close precedents; the contribution is incremental.

future_potential.positive: Controlled comparisons could clarify whether direct recent evidence improves sampled ranking beyond recurrent context and simple fixed fusion.
future_potential.negative: Latest-item shortcuts, redundant purchases and unobserved intent limit generality; no validation improvement or compatibility benefit has been established.

code_difficulty.positive: The selected module requires only small projections, norm control and a gate, with no new dataset or pretrained component.
code_difficulty.negative: Faithful padding correction, matched initialization and sampling, diagnostic adaptation, export consistency and budget accounting require substantial integration care.

related_work.title: PyTorch pack_padded_sequence and GRU documentation
contributions: Defines packed execution for variable-length recurrent inputs.
Supports excluding padded steps after chronological compaction of left-padded histories; GRU equations explain why zero embeddings alone do not freeze state.
limitations: Directly packing original left-padded tensors with valid lengths truncates real interactions.
Empty rows require separate handling, and aligned outputs must be restored for log2feats.
Does not establish recommendation accuracy or runtime gains.

related_work.title: Recurrent Neural Networks with Top-k Gains for Session-based Recommendations
contributions: Introduces BPR-max with negative-only softmax weighting and weighted negative-score regularization.
Provides the direct GRU4Rec precedent for the separate objective experiment.
Official implementation and sampling details are available at https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec_PyTorch_Official/master/gru4rec_pytorch.py.
limitations: Session-recommendation results do not establish gains under this Amazon protocol.
Filtering consumed items and deduplicating training candidates depart from official replacement-sampling semantics.
Loss aggregation, score regularization and sampling require separate matched controls.

related_work.title: Mamba4Rec: Towards Efficient Sequential Recommendation with Selective State Space Models
contributions: Studies selective state-space computation for sequential recommendation.
Motivates testing input-dependent weighting of sequential information.
limitations: Its backbone differs from GRU4Rec and cannot replace the required family.
Does not directly validate the proposed observed-item readout gate.

related_work.title: MARS: Attribute-aware text representations for recommendation
contributions: The supplied search summary describes attribute-aware representations that motivate finer item distinctions.
Inspires a deferred jointly trained title/description encoder.
limitations: Its pretrained-language-model setting does not establish effectiveness with randomly initialized text features.
Textual similarity cannot establish equipment compatibility, desired quantities or unmet purchase needs.

related_work.title: Neural Attentive Session-based Recommendation
contributions: Combines a final GRU state with attention-pooled recurrent states.
Provides close precedent for combining recent and broader sequential evidence.
limitations: Does not use the exact bounded projected-item interpolation proposed here.
Its results do not establish gains under the pinned four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: Hierarchical Gating Networks for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Uses feature-wise and item-wise gates for sequential recommendation.
Establishes gating as prior recommendation methodology.
limitations: Has no GRU backbone.
Does not isolate this learned coordinate-wise gate against tuned fixed fusion with identical projection and norm control.

related_work.title: Highway Networks
contributions: Provides the algebraic precedent for coordinate-wise interpolation using coupled transform and carry gates.
limitations: Does not establish recommendation-specific benefits or suitable branch scales.
A bounded gate alone does not bound the intervention relative to the recurrent feature norm.

related_work.title: Layer Normalization
contributions: Provides a possible mechanism for controlling branch activation scales.
limitations: Normalizing the recurrent branch changes the baseline representation.
Independent learned gains can restore scale imbalance; normalization does not establish coordinate alignment.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Explains why sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog evaluation.
Supports describing the pinned HR@10 specifically as sampled-candidate performance.
limitations: Does not authorize changing the host evaluator.
Does not supply a full-catalog improvement estimate for this experiment.

related_work.title: Accounting for Variance in Machine Learning Benchmarks
contributions: Highlights multiple sources of benchmark variability beyond a single fitted model.
Supports distinguishing user-resampling uncertainty from retraining and seed variability.
limitations: Bootstrap repetitions cannot substitute for independently trained models.
The mandated seed-42 experiment cannot estimate training-seed variability.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains selection optimism from repeated model selection on finite validation data.
Motivates prespecified comparison limits and cautious interpretation.
limitations: Ordinary post-selection bootstrap intervals do not correct adaptive selection.
Operational thresholds and category guardrails do not guarantee unbiased selection.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents paired resampling using shared indices across compared measurements.
Supports implementing conditional user-level uncertainty estimates when host outputs permit.
limitations: Valid resampling units and dependence structure must be specified by the experimenter.
Anonymous training rows cannot substitute for identified validation users, and cross-category identity dependence requires explicit handling.
